editorial:
Imagine living in a small, foggy village where the local boss is a cruel man who thinks he owns everyone. You get pulled into a dark story set in the 1800s where a land baron kills a group of Roma people, only to find out that some things should never be messed with. The vibe is heavy and creepy, making you feel like something is always watching from the trees. You follow the townspeople as they deal with bad dreams and missing kids, while a smart doctor tries to figure out if they are dealing with a wild beast or something way worse.

You will really like how the movie builds tension, though it moves a bit slow at first. The acting is solid, and the scenery makes the woods feel like a character of their own. One downside is that it doesn't have a ton of jump scares, so if you want a fast-paced slasher, this isn't it. However, if you like slow-burn mysteries, you should definitely check it out. It looks amazing in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you love owning movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The mystery wraps up when you realize the curse was real and targeted the baron's bloodline. The son didn't just disappear; he was taken by the spirits of the people his father killed. In the end, the cycle of violence catches up to the family. The town is left in ruins and the baron's legacy is destroyed, proving that the evil he started eventually came back to swallow him and his children whole.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gothic horror and stories about old curses.
